values.note: Three loops. The main loop has a group site, 4 double sites and pull-throughs; the horse loop (sites 32-36) has paddocks, hay racks, watering troughs, pull-throughs and a large trailer parking lot.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/woods-lake-campground-norwood-rd ('It has 3 loops with 41 campsites. The main loop has a group site, 4 double sites, and pull-through sites. The horse loop has 5 sites, 5 paddocks, 2 hay racks, watering troughs, pull-through sites and a large parking lot.'; 'Equestrian Sites (32-36)'), read 2026-10-28

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/woods-lake-campground-norwood-rd ('This site now has potable water.'; 'Restrooms: Vault toilet(s)'; 'Potable water is available at this site.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Equestrian sites $22. Additional vehicle $10-11, day use $6.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/woods-lake-campground-norwood-rd ('Single Site: $20 per night | Equestrian Site: $22 per night | Additional vehicle Fee: $10-11 per night'; '$6 per day for day use/picnic in a campsite'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Late spring to early fall, weather dependent. In 2026 the main campground closed September 30; the horse loop stays open free (no water) until November 3.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/woods-lake-campground-norwood-rd ('Seasons of Use: Late Spring to Early Fall - weather dependent'; 'Horse Loop Campground (6 sites) open for NO FEE until November 3rd, 2026, at 11 a.m. Trash and restrooms available. No water. Main campground is CLOSED for the season as of September 30th.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: First come, first served; pay on site, by recreation.gov Scan & Pay where available (download the app beforehand; little cell service).

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/gmug/recreation/woods-lake-campground-norwood-rd ('This site is a first come, first serve campground. Visit recreation.gov for more information.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10165751 ('This location is available on a first-come, first-served basis only. ... you may be able to pay for your campsite(s) by scanning a QR code using the Recreation.gov mobile app'; rules scanAndPay 'S&P Only'), read 2026-10-28

note: In aspen forest at ~9,400 ft next to Woods Lake, below the Lizard Head Wilderness, between Placerville and Telluride: from CO-145 2.4 miles east of Placerville, 7.4 miles up Fall Creek Road (FR 618), then about 2 miles on FR 621. Sites are set back in the trees; the lake (fishing) is a short walk. Trailheads for the Woods Lake and Lone Cone trails into the wilderness; Wilson Mesa Trail half a mile away. --Claude
